title: Lesson 7.5: Compliance & Auditing the Recovery Plan

story.vex: A plan nobody's tested is worth exactly nothing when I actually attack. (Commander Vex, Planet Doom)
story.victory: DOOM ATTACK REPELLED before it started: every non-compliant plan is caught in the audit, not discovered during a real crisis. Astro: "Written isn't tested. The audit is how we tell the difference."

files.C:\\Citadel\\README.txt:
ORDERS FROM ASTRO
=================
Read audit-standard.txt for the requirement, then test-records.txt for four systems. Classify each as compliant or non-compliant.

1. type audit-standard.txt
2. type test-records.txt
3. classify <system> compliant | non-compliant
files.C:\\Citadel\\audit-standard.txt:
AUDIT STANDARD
----------------
Every DR plan must be tested within the last 12 months, with a written record of the test.
files.C:\\Citadel\\test-records.txt:
TEST RECORDS
--------------
system-relay              tested 4 months ago, written record on file
system-shield-generator   plan written and detailed, but never actually tested
system-starmap-vault      tested 15 months ago, written record on file (over 12 months old)
system-comms-backup       tested 2 months ago, written record on file

steps.title: Volt's Drill: read the standard and records
steps.body: Volt: "Know the requirement, then check the evidence." `type audit-standard.txt`, then `type test-records.txt`.

steps.title: Audit each system
steps.body: Volt: "Tested within 12 months, with a record — compliant. Never tested, or the record is too old — non-compliant." Classify all four systems.

objectives.label: system-starmap-vault classified as non-compliant (record too old)
